properties.description:
The `help` skill: what reflow2 physically is, what it can answer that nothing else can, the one first move for where the person actually is, and what it deliberately will not do. Served and mirrored, reachable by `/what-is-this`.

DISTINCT FROM `cap:explains-itself`, WHICH IT DOES NOT REPLACE. That capability is the DOCUMENTATION entry surface — README, getting-started, diagrams — and reaches a stranger who lands on the repository with no agent at all. This one reaches the person who has an agent and asks it. Two audiences, two surfaces, and the README is the one a stranger meets first, so `req:explains-itself` is satisfied only PARTIALLY here and BL-102 stays open.

DISTINCT FROM `cap:onboarding`, one question earlier. That answers "where does this new work belong" for someone new to a DESIGN; this answers "what is this thing" for someone new to the TOOL.

⭐ SECTION 2 IS THE POINT AND IS THE ONE MOST LIKELY TO BE LEFT OUT. A tool described by its checks reads as a linter, and a person who thinks reflow2 is a linter never asks it the questions it exists for. So the skill names four things it can answer that nothing else can — how much of what we said we would build actually works (computed from the thread, not from a status field), why it is like this and WHO decided, what breaks if I change this, and where does new work belong. This is `fact:the-instruction-surface-routes-to-hygiene-and-not-to-whether-the-thing-works` applied at first contact rather than at orientation.

⚠️ AND IT STATES THE COST IN THE SAME BREATH: reflow2 only knows what somebody told it, and the work of capture is real. Hiding that produces a user who feels misled in week two.

SECTION 4 IS THE OTHER HALF OF THAT HONESTY — four things it deliberately will NOT do, said unprompted: it does not read source and build the design for you, it does not decide anything for you, it does not judge whether a check is meaningful, and it cannot tell you the design matches reality. Each is a deliberate choice rather than a missing feature, and each is a week-two disappointment otherwise.

📌 IT ALSO CORRECTS A STALE CLAUSE IN THE REQUIREMENT. `req:explains-itself` says a newcomer must "find where the agent instructions go". Since the user-scope installer there is nowhere to put them — install once per machine and every project is registered, with no per-project setup and no file to place. The skill answers the question by saying there is nothing to do, which is the true and more useful answer.
properties.name: Someone who has never seen reflow2 can ask their agent what it is and get a straight answer
